newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - TV producer Endemol seeks foreign growth.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - TV producer Endemol seeks foreign growth.

text.p: Dutch television production company Endemol Entertainment reported a sharp rise in profits on Friday and said it would continue to focus on expansion outside its core Dutch and German markets in the coming years.

Endemol, which plans a partial flotation of its shares on the Amsterdam bourse later this year, said net profit for the 1995/96 financial year to July 31 rose over 38 percent to 60.5 million guilders ($35.4 million) from 43.7 million.
It attributed the rise in earnings both to organic growth and acquisitions, notably the purchase of the internationally operating Holiday on Ice skating show.
The company said net profit would rise by 15 to 20 percent in the current 1996/97 financial year, adding that it expected both sales and profits to double within five years.
Endemol, which posted 1995/96 sales of 642.4 million guilders, said it planned further expansion abroad.
"Foreign markets are becoming increasingly important for us," joint-chairman John de Mol told a news conference.
De Mol noted that over 40 percent of the company's television programming turnover was already generated outside the Netherlands, with some 30 percent coming from Germany alone.
"All the other European countries together contribute only 11 percent. I say 'only' because that is where we believe our best prospects for growth lie," he said.
Production of television programmes accounts for just under 80 percent of Endemol's sales, with the rest generated by the company's live entertainment division.
Formed in 1994 through a merger of the TV production firms of joint chairmen Joop van den Ende and John de Mol, Endemol specialises in popular game shows, soap operas and drama series.

Its main television operations outside the Netherlands include wholly-owned production subsidiaries in Germany and Portugal as well as joint ventures in Spain and France in which it holds stakes of 40 and 50 percent respectively.
De Mol said Endemol viewed eastern Europe as one of the most promising growth markets.

But Endemol is optimistic about the opportunities throughout Europe as the ending of state monopolies leads to the growth of independent TV channels who are increasingly looking to replace cheap imported U.S. shows with programmes in their own language.
"We see growth of the television market in Europe because the market is maturing. There is a growing need for locally produced prime-time amusement," De Mol said.
Endemol also plans to expand its live entertainment business, in some cases through co-productions with foreign partners, he said.
Live entertainment, which includes Holiday on Ice and the production of Broadway- or West End-style musicals in the Netherlands, accpounts for 21 percent of annual sales.
Endemol's stage production of the Dutch version of the Phantom of the Opera ran for an unprecedented three years.
De Mol said Endemol's Dutch version of Miss Saigon would open in six weeks, adding that advance ticket sales were double those for the Phantom six weeks before that show opened. ($1=1.709 Guilder)
